title: Open problem: Does exposure to the expected value — an analyst's knowledge of a preexisting recommended
statement: Does exposure to the expected value — an analyst's knowledge of a preexisting recommended value — degrade the calibration of quoted uncertainties in a series of physics measurements of the same quantity? Posed in print in 1986 with its predicted signature named, and never estimated. Any test must estimate herding and calibration JOINTLY per stratum rather than excluding the central-value limb by assertion: this is the ledger's own algebra, not a cited result — the squared bias enters E[p^2] for a normalised residual, so a calibration factor fitted on pulls cannot be made independent of the central value by declaring it so. Computable part on public data: the two-reference decomposition — chi-square of normalised residuals against the contemporaneous published average AND against the final value, per quantity, which Klein & Roodman did for four quantities — run over the Review of Particle Physics measurement histories, Bailey's Dryad dataset (doi 10.5061/dryad.jb3mj), Croft & Dailey's 637 cosmological measurements and Lopez-Corredoira's H0 series. Report a robust per-stratum scale (a Student-t scale or the median absolute pull) alongside the variance multiplier first, because the factor is outlier-dominated in this corpus family. Do NOT re-run the marginal calibration: it is published several times over (Birge ratios 1.2-3.0; Bailey's tail index near 2-3; Croft & Dailey's factor of about 2 before 2000, with supernova errors recently OVERestimated at N_sigma 0.5 +/- 0.07 and 0.77 +/- 0.12, a direction reversal inside the same corpus). NOT part of this row: the central-value limb (does blinding de-bias the mean?). It looks routable on the same two sources, but the sentences that would pose it were not verbatim-verified by this ledger's checking pass, and a row's posing sentence is quoted from the paper rather than from an adversary's summary. It is recorded here as a candidate row awaiting that check. Provenance: located at Gate 2 and Gate 4 of UQ-20261017-05 and corrected by its verification pass.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: Henrion M, Fischhoff B, "Assessing uncertainty in physical constants", *Am. J. Phys.* 54(9):791-798 (1986), doi 10.1119/1.14447 — opened in full and verified verbatim: "Having a preexisting recommended value may particularly encourage investigators to discard or adjust unexpected results, and so induce correlated errors in apparently independent experiments." and "The result would be initially small Birge ratios, unduly tight confidence intervals, and the exclusion of discrepant data." They pose the mechanism and do not estimate it: there is no exposed-versus-unexposed arm anywhere in the paper. What they do measure is pooled calibration — Birge ratio, interquartile index and surprise index over the speed of light (27 values, 1875-1958), G (14 values), the proton magnetic moment, the inverse fine-structure constant, the ohm ratio, and 306 Particle Data Group lifetimes and meson masses — concluding "Reported uncertainties are too small." CORRECTION to an earlier draft of this row: the remedy they propose is referee-blind review, not analysis blinding — "referees might be asked to scrutinize the account of an experiment 'blind,' before knowing its outcome and whether it affirmed prior expectations." Blinding the analyst to the recommended value is this ledger's operationalisation, not theirs. Klein JR, Roodman A, *Annu. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci.* 55:141-163 (2005) report no blinded-versus-unblinded calibration comparison; their one quantitative item is a clustering check on four historical unblinded series — "the measurements do tend to cluster nearer the prior published averages than the final value", with chi-square "131.2 for 83 degrees of freedom" about the prior averages against "249.7" about the final average. The words "pull" and "normalized residual" do not appear in what could be read, so the pull-variance argument in the Problem column is this ledger's derivation, and the factors it implies (1.26 against 1.73) are the ledger's arithmetic on those two printed chi-squares. Croft RAC & Dailey M, arXiv:1112.3108, opened and verified: "The total number of parameter measurements in the 20 year period shown is 637", 12 cosmological parameters 1990-2010 scraped from ADS abstracts, endpoint N_sigma against a WMAP7 fiducial, "consistent with an average underestimate of the error bars by a factor of ~2" before 2000 and "results in the last 10 years are consistent with expectations"; blinding appears only as a recommendation — "Wider use of blind analyses in cosmology could help to avoid this" — and never as a measured covariate. So the era- and method-stratified version of this analysis exists and is one covariate short, fifteen years on.
inputs.tier: A for the two-reference herding-plus-calibration decomposition on the existing public compilations, which are already assembled and public. The blinding-coded exposure arm is C: it needs hand-coding of analysis protocol from hundreds of primary papers with inconsistent pre-2000 reporting, and it is collinear with the factor-of-two era shift Croft & Dailey document at the same boundary where blinding spread, so the era confound has to be addressed in the design rather than adjusted away afterwards.
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
